items.title: Fahmi acknowledges PKR delegates' concerns over government communication strategy
items.summary: AYЕR KEROH: PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has acknowledged concerns raised by party delegates over the government's communication strategy, particularly the difficulty in translating macroeconomic achievements into benefits felt at the household level. Fahmi said the issue was among the key messages emerging midway through the 2026 PKR National Congress, with delegates calling for improvements to the party's machinery, as well as its communication and information strategies. Fahmi, who is also communications minister, said the party leadership was taking the feedback seriously and was prepared to make changes.

items.title: Motac cracks down on unlicensed tourism operators in KL, issues 15 notices
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — The Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (Motac) issued 15 inspection notices for various offences under the Tourism Industry Act 1992 (Act 482) during a two-day enforcement operation that began on Wednesday around Kuala Lumpur. In a statement today, Motac said nine of the notices were issued under Subsection 5(2) for operating a tourism business without a valid licence. “Three tourist locations, nine business premises and three individuals were inspected over the course of the operation.

items.title: Federal govt aims to cut Terengganu poor households to 20,000 by year-end
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 15 — The federal government aims to reduce the number of poor households in Terengganu to 20,000 by this December. Deputy director-general of the Strategic Development, Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU), under the Prime Minister’s Department (ICU JPM), Datuk Norashiken Ishak, said as of August 13, the number of poor households in Terengganu was recorded at 24,100 households, compared to 26,800 households in early July. She also said the total includes 161 new construction projects, 146 house renovation projects, and three new stilt house construction projects.

items.title: Flores earthquake: No Malaysians affected, says embassy
items.summary: JAKARTA: No Malaysians have been reported affected by the magnitude 7.7 earthquake that struck Flores in Indonesia's East Nusa Tenggara (NTT) province early Saturday. The Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta said it had contacted Malaysians in NTT who were registered with the embassy, as well as Malaysian tourists who had informed the embassy of their whereabouts in the region. Malaysians affected by the earthquake and requiring consular assistance can contact the Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta at +62 813 8081 3036 or email mwjakarta@kln.gov.my.

items.title: KDM withdraws support for GRS, says Priscella
items.summary: KDM president Priscella Peter said the decision was made unanimously by the party's supreme council, taking into account the party's interests and the need to rebuild public confidence at the grassroots. She said the decision was not easy but necessary to give the party a clear direction and demonstrate that KDM was committed to engaging with voters beyond election periods. Priscella said developments following the previous election had affected the party and were among the factors behind its decision to move outside the GRS government.

items.title: Sabah hospital sexual harassment case: MOH moves director out, complainant under treatment, PSD to decide next step
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — The Health Ministry has completed its internal investigation into an alleged sexual harassment case involving a Sabah hospital director and transferred the officer to a medical post at the Sabah Health Department. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry had also submitted its report to the Public Service Department (PSD), which has jurisdiction over further action based on the officer’s grade, The New Straits Times reported. “Administratively, the ministry has completed the internal investigation.

items.title: Five PKR figures honoured with posthumous awards
items.summary: Four received the Bill Kayong Award, while the fifth was awarded the Dr Syed Husin Ali Pejuang Rakyat Award, introduced for the first time in recognition of the late Syed Husin’s contributions as a PKR founder and advocate of social justice. The Bill Kayong Award was presented to the late Sapiah Zaini, former Miri Women’s chief; the late Hasbul Syafiqi Hasbullah, Keadilan Penang working secretary; and party activists, the late Syafiq Ali Abdullah@Abang Mani, and the late Muhammad Shahhanaz Nazarudin. The award, named after the late Sarawak activist Bill Kayong, recognises individuals who have made significant contributions to the party’s struggle and grassroots work.

items.title: AUKU abolition must involve students, academics, civil society, says youth NGO
items.summary: Its coordinator, Hamdin Nordin, said the Higher Education Ministry should also ensure wider stakeholder participation in drafting a new legal framework for the governance of higher education institutions. He said the government's announcement to abolish AUKU was an important step towards strengthening democracy and freedom in higher education institutions. Hamdin said the ministry should ensure the new legislation was drafted inclusively, with the participation of students, academics and civil society.

items.title: 10 Lojing vegetable farming firms issued DOE notices over EIA breaches
items.summary: GUA MUSANG: The Kelantan Department of Environment (DOE) has issued notices to 10 vegetable farming companies in Lojing Highlands for violating environmental requirements. The notices were issued under Sections 31 and 37 of the Environmental Quality Act 1974 for breaches of conditions imposed under approved Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs), including land clearance and planting activities. "DOE officers inspected vegetable farms in Lojing Highlands, and 10 operators who failed to comply with conditions imposed under their approved EIAs were issued notices under Sections 31 and 37 of the Environmental Quality Act 1974.

items.title: MOH to reopen four training institutes next year amid critical nurse shortage
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is strengthening three key strategies under the country’s health workforce reform to address the critical shortage of nurses, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad. He said the three strategies involved increasing the number of nursing graduates, expanding career pathways and implementing direct recruitment and greater autonomy in staffing management. Dzulkefly said the move was important in meeting the country’s health workforce needs amid the increasingly complex challenges facing the health system.

items.title: India envoy urges Malaysian Indians to preserve roots
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Indians in Malaysia have been urged to uphold their cultural roots while contributing to the country they call home and strengthening longstanding ties between India and Malaysia. India's Charge d'Affaires to Malaysia, Shri Hitesh Rajpal, said the Indian community, including professionals, students, workers, entrepreneurs, families and elders, remained an integral part of the larger Indian family. He also called for stronger people-to-people ties, greater economic cooperation and mutual support between India and Malaysia.

items.title: Subang Airport runway reopens after temporary closure following helicopter fire
items.summary: SUBANG: The runway at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport here, which was temporarily closed following a helicopter fire earlier today, has reopened. Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) chief executive officer Captain Datuk Norazman Mahmud said the runway was reopened following the incident at Taxiway Victor. CAAM earlier said the airport's runway had been closed, with all flights put on hold until further notice.

items.title: Onn Hafiz: Bangsa Johor rental deposit aid of RM1,000 to roll out next year
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 15 — The Johor government is expected to introduce the RM1,000 Bangsa Johor rental deposit assistance next year to help people in the state who face difficulties coming up with the upfront payment for accommodation. They serve in Johor, are part of Bangsa Johor and are working for us,” he said. Onn Hafiz said the first phase of the rental deposit assistance would target about 10,000 recipients.

items.title: DoE detects seven hotspots in East Malaysia as transboundary haze worsens air quality
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — A total of seven hotspots were detected in the country, with five in Sarawak and two in Sabah, as air quality deteriorates in several areas of Sarawak, which are currently recording Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels. “Moderate to dense localised smoke plumes were also observed, originating from hotspots in large parts of Kalimantan, central Sarawak and central Sumatra,” she said in a statement today. She said several air quality monitoring stations in West Kalimantan as well as western and central Sarawak also recorded unhealthy readings.

items.title: Sabah-based KDM cuts ties with GRS govt, says it’s time to win back grassroots
items.summary: KINARUT, Aug 15 — Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM) today pulled its support for the Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS)-led state government, signalling a shift in the party’s political direction ahead of the next general election. KDM acting president Priscella Peter said the decision was made by the party’s supreme council during its annual meeting today, local media reported. Priscella said the party had been affected by what happened after the previous state election, prompting it to make its position known well before the next polls.

items.title: Defence Capacity Blueprint 2026–2030: Building Malaysia's defence beyond military assets
items.summary: However, in today's increasingly complex security environment, military hardware alone can no longer determine a country's defence readiness. This broader understanding of defence is what underpins Malaysia's Defence Capacity Blueprint (RTKP) 2026 – 2030. However, building defence capacity extends beyond developing capable defence professionals.

items.title: If you’re naughty, we will know it, mayor warns as Kota Kinabalu adds 1,600 CCTV cameras to catch vandals
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — A total of 1,600 closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras will be installed across the city soon as City Hall (DBKK) moves to strengthen surveillance and protect public assets from vandalism. Sabin also said the Kota Kinabalu International Mayors’ Dialogue 2026 would bring together mayors, city leaders, policymakers, development partners and other stakeholders to exchange ideas and practical experiences on the challenges and opportunities facing cities. He said Australian participation would provide an opportunity to strengthen practical cooperation and relationships between Kota Kinabalu and Australian cities, and expressed hope that the Australian High Commission could help facilitate the attendance of Australian city leaders.

items.title: Tourism Ministry cracks down on unlicensed operators in KL
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry issued 15 inspection notices for various offences under the Tourism Industry Act 1992 during a two-day enforcement operation around Kuala Lumpur that began on Wednesday. In a statement today, the ministry said nine of the notices were issued under Subsection 5(2) for operating a tourism business without a valid licence. "Intelligence work in collaboration with the Kuala Lumpur Tourist Guide Association (KLTGA) was also carried out to detect individuals suspected of carrying out tourist guide activities without valid licences.

items.title: Tawau drone medicine pilot identifies two landing sites
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Health Ministry and Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) are preparing a pilot medication-drone delivery service in Tawau, with the launch and landing sites identified. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the launch site had been identified at Tawau Health Clinic, while landing sites had been identified at MCMC's National Information Dissemination Centre (Nadi) centres in Sungai Imam and Tinagat. items.title: Hospital director transferred over sexual harassment probe, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Health Ministry has taken administrative action against a hospital director in Sabah following an internal investigation into an alleged sexual harassment case. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the former director had been transferred to the Sabah Health Department as a medical officer, pending further action. On mental health, especially involving students in schools, Dzulkefly said no single ministry could address various health and public health challenges alone.

items.title: Seven hotspots detected in Malaysia as haze worsens in Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of seven hotspots were detected in the country, with five in Sarawak and two in Sabah, as air quality deteriorated in several areas of Sarawak, which recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings. Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said that, based on the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) report dated Aug 14, a total of 226 hotspots were also detected in Kalimantan, while another five were recorded in Sumatra. She said several air quality monitoring stations in West Kalimantan as well as western and central Sarawak also recorded unhealthy readings.

items.title: Threat ends as Sabah wildlife officers kill 14-foot croc near in Sipitang river near jetty to Labuan
items.summary: SIPITANG, August 15 — A 14-foot male crocodile was caught and shot dead by the Sabah Wildlife Department (JHL) on Thursday, bringing relief to residents who had been living in fear of the reptile at Kampung Tanjung Pagar. The crocodile was frequently spotted at the mouth of the river near Kg Tanjung Pagar before it was shot dead and handed over to a licensed crocodile hunter. However, residents have been warned to remain cautious as other crocodiles could still be in the area.

items.title: Explainer: What abolishing AUKU means for universities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has announced that the government will abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU). Originally introduced to regulate the establishment and administration of public universities, AUKU later became associated with restrictions on student activism and political activities on campuses, particularly following amendments in the mid-1970s. The Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Act 30) was enacted to provide the legal framework for the establishment, governance and administration of public universities and university colleges in Malaysia.

items.title: 2027 Budget to focus on expanding AI adoption, says Gobind
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will focus on expanding the use of artificial intelligence (AI), including exploring systems to promote wider access to AI tools, in the 2027 Budget to be tabled in October. Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said AI Malaysia, launched three weeks ago by the Digital Ministry, would require significant funding to mobilise expertise and develop AI infrastructure to support its adoption across sectors. "Beyond experts, we also need to build AI infrastructure that can support every sector in Malaysia and drive the technology forward.

items.title: Finance Ministry to roll out RM1.2b in STR cash aid for 5.3 million recipients from today
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 15 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) said Phase 3 payments of the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid will be disbursed in stages starting today to 5.3 million recipients, with an allocation of RM1.2 billion. Of these, 3.9 million are low- and middle-income households, and 1.4 million are single senior citizens. The ministry said, depending on the category they fall under, recipients can collect up to RM3,300 in total by August 2026, combining STR Phases 1 to 3 and the monthly SARA basic aid.

items.title: 'That's my wife and son': Husband's fears confirmed after tanker crash
items.summary: TEMERLOH: "That is my wife and son," were the words that flashed through Saifulnizam Sulaiman's mind after learning of a horrific crash involving a car and a fuel tanker lorry at Km9 of Jalan Temerloh-Triang near Kampung Lebak yesterday. Saifulnizam, 39, said his wife Nur Fatima Syuhada Abdullah, 39, and their son Muhamad Fattah Aisy, 12, were travelling from Jerantut to Seremban, Negri Sembilan, when the crash occurred. He said he learned of the incident through social media and immediately felt the victims were his wife and son.

items.title: Tengku Mahkota Pahang makes history as first royal to complete RMAF helicopter course
items.summary: ALOR STAR: Tengku Mahkota Pahang Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah created history as the first royal family member to complete the Basic Helicopter Flying Course Series 67 (A)/26 at the Air Force College (KTU) here. Tengku Hassanal was among 39 participants who completed flight training and received their Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) Flying Wings. The ceremony involved graduates from four flight courses, namely the Basic Helicopter Flying Course Series 67(A)/26, Basic Helicopter Flying Course Series 67/25, Basic Flying Course Series 87/25, and Fighter Weapon Sensor Officer Basic Course Series 01/25.

items.title: Ukrainian crew member injured by debris in Subang helicopter fire
items.summary: SUBANG: A Ukrainian crew member was lightly injured after being struck by debris when a helicopter caught fire at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport here today. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said information from the Airport Fire and Rescue Service indicated the injured man was outside the helicopter when he was hit by flying debris. Firefighters from the Airport Fire and Rescue Service and the Bukit Jelutong Fire and Rescue Station were deployed to the scene.

items.title: PKR delegates question Umno sincerity and loyalty as Unity Government partner
items.summary: Selangor PKR delegate Danish Hairudin said the two polls had exposed what he described as Umno's lack of sincerity and solidarity, despite both parties being part of the Unity Government. He said political cooperation, while necessary for stability, should not come at the expense of PKR's interests or dignity. "In Johor, Umno stabbed us.

items.title: He saw the crash online and knew something was wrong: Father loses wife, son in Temerloh crash
items.summary: TEMERLOH, Aug 15 — A routine wait for his wife’s arrival turned into a frantic search for answers after Saifulnizam Sulaiman realised she had not responded to his messages or calls for hours. Saifulnizam, 39, was in Seremban for work while his wife, Nur Fatima Syuhada Abdullah, 39, and their 12-year-old son, Muhammad Fattah Aisy Naufal Saifulnizam, were travelling from Jerantut to join him during the school holidays. His worst fears grew after he came across social media posts about a crash along Jalan Temerloh-Triang.

items.title: Fuel tanker driver remanded over crash that killed mother and son in Temerloh
items.summary: TEMERLOH: The fuel tanker driver involved in a fatal crash that claimed the lives of a mother and her son at Km9 of Jalan Temerloh-Triang near Kampung Lebak yesterday has been remanded for four days to assist in investigations. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said the 37-year-old man was remanded from today until Tuesday. The tanker driver sustained minor injuries.

items.title: Phase 3 STR cash aid payout begins today for 5.3 million recipients
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Finance Ministry will disburse Phase 3 payments of the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid in stages starting today to 5.3 million recipients, involving an allocation of RM1.2 billion. The number of recipients has grown by 300,000 since the start of the year, when it stood at five million, comprising 3.9 million low- and middle-income households and 1.4 million single senior citizens. The ministry said recipients could receive up to RM3,300 in total by August 2026 across STR Phases 1 to 3 and monthly Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) basic aid, excluding the one-off Sara payment for citizens aged 18 and above.

items.title: PKFZ rejects link between Chinese cargo and tariff evasion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Port Klang Free Zone (PKFZ) said the presence of Chinese-linked businesses or international cargo within a Malaysian free zone should not, in itself, be interpreted as evidence of tariff evasion or illegal transshipment. PKFZ chairman Lim Lip Eng said the free zone operated within a highly regulated customs and trade compliance framework as an integrated logistics hub. He said all investors, manufacturers, traders and logistics operators seeking to establish operations within PKFZ were subject to stringent screening, due diligence and regulatory requirements.

items.title: New ‘One Higher Education Act’, launched in January, to replace UUCA, Zambry confirms
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 15 — A more comprehensive national higher education legislative framework to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA) has been outlined under the Malaysia Higher Education Plan (RPTM) 2026-2035, said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir. He said the effort was part of the agenda for establishing the One Higher Education Act, which was launched in January 2026. Zambry said the Higher Education Ministry was taking into account the need to reform the national higher education legislative framework by drafting a new, more comprehensive act to replace UUCA.

items.title: Subang Airport flights suspended after helicopter catches fire during test
items.summary: SUBANG: All flights to and from Subang Airport here have been suspended after a Kamov Ka-32S helicopter caught fire during an engine ground run today. The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said the helicopter, registered as UR-CIT, caught fire at 12.28pm while undergoing an engine test as part of maintenance activities. Earlier, the Selangor Fire and Rescue Department said four people escaped unhurt after the helicopter caught fire while preparing for take-off for the engine test following repairs.

items.title: Helicopter catches fire during engine test at Subang airport, four escape but one hit by debris
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, Aug 15 — A Kamov Ka-32 helicopter caught fire during an engine test at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport here today, with four people escaping and one person reportedly injured after being struck by debris outside the aircraft. “The fire occurred as the helicopter was about to take off for the purpose of engine testing after repairs,” Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said in a statement today. Five firefighters from the Bukit Jelutong Fire and Rescue Station were deployed with a Fire Rescue Tender to the scene.

items.title: King told govt not to stop at TH, turn attention to Felda, says Anwar
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said the government will uncover alleged governance failures within the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda), which has been burdened by substantial debt. Anwar, who is also PKR president, said the move was not aimed at punishing anyone prematurely, but at establishing the facts and ensuring that any wrongdoing was properly investigated. He said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had also instructed that investigations into governance failures should not end with Lembaga Tabung Haji.

items.title: MoH: No significant rise in haze-related illnesses yet
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 15 — Malaysia has not recorded a significant increase in haze-related illnesses so far, but the Ministry of Health (MOH) does not rule out a rise in cases if air quality worsens or the haze persists. The MOH said no increase had been recorded so far in the three types of haze-related illnesses, namely upper respiratory tract infections (URTI), asthma and conjunctivitis, monitored through sentinel health facilities. In Sarawak, the MOH said monitoring at 12 sentinel health clinics recorded a decline in URTI cases, from 1,473 in Epidemiological Week (EW) 31, before the haze, to 1,347 in EW 32.

items.title: MACC detains seven in Tabung Haji RCI probe, including senior executives and shipping company CEO
items.summary: According to sources, the suspects, comprising a chief executive officer, a former director, a director and four former TH senior executives, were arrested separately between 3pm and 10.30pm last night at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya. “The first suspect, a shipping company CEO with a ‘Datuk’ title in his 60s, was arrested on suspicion of submitting documents with false details when making payments to TH. “The second suspect is a construction company director with a ‘Datuk’ title, also in his 60s.

items.title: Penang PH-BN cooperation based on consensus, including DAP, says Chow
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: The decision to maintain cooperation between Pakatan Harapan and Barisan Nasional in Penang was made through a consensus among all component parties, including DAP, says Penang PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow. He said there was no issue regarding the decision as it reflected the stance of the respective parties and was endorsed by the Penang PH Leadership Council. However, he said Penang DAP chairman Steven Sim had presented the party's stance on the matter during the state PH meeting.

items.title: Anwar signals key changes before Budget 2027, first announcements due Monday
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he would soon announce several urgent changes that the government plans to implement before the tabling of Budget 2027 in early October. He said the changes would involve government policies, internal issues within Pakatan Harapan (PH) and cooperation among parties in the federal unity government. Anwar, who is PKR president, said he would begin sharing details of some of the changes from the day after tomorrow, ahead of Merdeka Day and Malaysia Day celebrations.

items.title: ‘I take the peaceful path’: Anwar dismisses Khairy’s claim of rift with Zahid
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has stressed that his relationship with Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi remains good. He said former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin’s claim that their relationship had deteriorated was merely the former Rembau Member of Parliament’s personal view. Anwar, who is also PKR president and Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman, said he had also expressed his appreciation in his speech at the congress for the role played by Ahmad Zahid, as Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman and Umno president, in facilitating the formation of the Unity Government following the 15th General Election (GE15).

items.title: New Act to replace AUKU, says Zambry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A new, more comprehensive Act will be introduced to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU), said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir. He said efforts to reform the higher education legal framework had been outlined in the Malaysia Higher Education Plan 2026–2035, launched in January, through the One Higher Education Act agenda. Zambry said the abolition of AUKU must be followed by a new legal framework that is more comprehensive, progressive and suited to the needs of higher education today and in the future.

items.title: Penang Pakatan’s decision to stay with BN had component parties’ consensus, says Chow Kon Yeow
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Aug 15 — Penang Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) decision to maintain its cooperation with Barisan Nasional (BN) was reached by consensus among all its component parties, including DAP, state PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow reportedly said today. According to Berita Harian , Chow said the respective positions of DAP, PKR and Amanah had been presented before the state PH Leadership Council endorsed the continued partnership. He said Sim, Penang Amanah chairman Muhammad Faiz Fadzil and state PKR Leadership Council chairman Datuk Dr Mohamad Abdul Hamid had expressed the same position, leading PH to retain the cooperation.

items.title: Pas says GE16 could be held anytime amid PH-BN tensions, Melaka polls
items.summary: TUMPAT: Pas believes several factors could result in the 16th General Election (GE16) being held at any time, including the expiry of the Melaka state assembly's term and ties between Pakatan Harapan and Barisan Nasional. Pas vice-president Datuk Idris Ahmad said the situation should serve as a wake-up call to all parties to be prepared for the possibility of an early election. Describing the relationship as lukewarm, Idris said recent political developments indicated that cooperation between the two coalitions could face challenges.

items.title: Four escape unhurt after helicopter catches fire at Subang Airport [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Four people escaped unhurt after a helicopter caught fire while preparing to take off for an engine test following repairs at Subang Airport today. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 12.30pm and arrived at the scene four minutes later. "The helicopter was fully engulfed in flames when firefighters arrived, with airport fire and rescue service personnel and firefighters immediately carrying out firefighting operations," he said when contacted.

items.title: AUKU abolition victory for student movement, says PKR Youth chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's decision to abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) has been described as a significant step towards restoring freedom and democratic space for university students. Welcoming the announcement by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim said it was an important victory in the decades-long student movement for a freer and more democratic campus environment. items.title: Urgent government changes to be announced starting late August, says Anwar
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will make several announcements regarding urgent changes to be implemented by the government starting late this month, culminating in the tabling of 2027 Budget in early October. The prime minister, who is also Pakatan Harapan chairman, said the announcements would cover government policies, internal PH matters, cooperation within the unity government, and national programmes. Also present were PKR and unity government leaders, including PKR deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar, Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) chairman Datuk Seri Hajiji Nor, and Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.

items.title: Anwar may make more announcements as early as tomorrow, says Fahmi
items.summary: AYER KEROH: PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim may make several more announcements as early as tomorrow. He said this as the party leadership considers proposals raised by delegates at the 2026 PKR National Congress, following Anwar's statement that the government would abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU). Fahmi said the party leadership would take into account the views and proposals raised by delegates and consider how they could be translated into action.

items.title: Anwar: UUCA repeal proposal goes to Cabinet next week
items.summary: AYER KEROH, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today his proposal to repeal the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA) will be brought to the Cabinet next Wednesday for consideration. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the Cabinet would need to deliberate on his proposal first, Berita Harian reported when reporters asked if the repeal had already been approved. Anwar had earlier announced during his speech that the government would repeal UUCA, citing continued objections from university students among the reasons for the move.

items.title: PKR Youth backs UUCA repeal, urges students to speak up for wider reforms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — PKR Youth today backed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement to repeal the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), but said the move should pave the way for wider reforms to strengthen university autonomy, academic freedom and student rights. The party’s youth wing also urged students to continue speaking up and acting as a check and balance on the government, despite being part of Anwar’s own party. “To Malaysian students, do not stop speaking up.

items.title: Anwar announces special Madani F1 tickets for MyKad holders from RM200
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Malaysians holding MyKad will be able to attend all three days of Formula 1’s return to Sepang through special Tiket Madani priced from RM200, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today. He said the initiative would give more Malaysians the opportunity to experience Formula 1 in person when the race returns to Sepang in October. Anwar said the initiative was aimed at giving more Malaysians the chance to experience Formula 1 directly at Sepang.

items.title: Anwar says allocations for Sabah, Sarawak, Kedah and Kelantan increased under Madani govt
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today dismissed claims by certain quarters that the Madani Government is sidelining several states. “Terengganu’s allocation rose from RM6 billion in 2022 to RM8.1 billion this year, as did Perlis, Johor and others. Anwar said the Federal allocation to Sabah had also increased by 35 per cent, from RM13 billion in 2022 to RM17.6 billion in 2026, while Sarawak’s allocation rose from RM10.2 billion in 2022 to RM15.1 billion, an increase of 48 per cent.

items.title: Missing three days, found 140km away, back with families but KL police still investigating case of two Alor Gajah MRSM students
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Two 16-year-old MRSM Alor Gajah students who went missing for three days have been reunited with their families. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the two teenagers were found at about 10.30pm yesterday at Central Market here — nearly 140km away from the Melaka school campus. The students, Siti Nur Aaira Aidi and Nur Aisy Humaira Mohd Saad, were reported missing after a teacher lodged a police report at 10.46pm on August 11.

items.title: Not all of Umno can be guilty: Pakatan Harapan should not use an overly generic approach – Phar Kim Beng
items.summary: The principle should be straightforward: not all of Umno can be guilty simply because some Umno leaders, office-holders or political appointees may have been implicated in wrongdoing. Investigations must identify particular decisions, particular offices, particular individuals and particular periods. Umno is not one person.

items.title: Anwar on Tabung Haji RCI findings: ‘RM12b was lost, isn’t that sakau?’
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has stressed that acts of “sakau” (siphoning of funds) did occur in Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), following the loss of billions of ringgit as highlighted in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the institution. “Some people do not like the term ‘sakau’. Meanwhile, the Prime Minister said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim.

items.title: Anwar announces repeal of Universities and University Colleges Act, after students push for greater freedom
items.summary: AYER KEROH, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today announced that the government will repeal the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), following continued calls from students for greater freedom. Anwar, who is also PKR president, said the decision came after several amendments to the Act failed to address all concerns raised by university students, local media reported. The 2024 amendments also shifted disciplinary decisions involving public university students from the vice-chancellor to Student Disciplinary Committees through amendments to Section 16B.

items.title: Woman rescued by public after falling from Darul Hana Bridge in Kuching
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 15 — A woman was rescued by members of the public after falling from the Darul Hana Bridge at Kuching Waterfront here yesterday evening. “Initial investigations found that the incident was related to a personal issue — however, investigations are ongoing to determine the root cause of the incident. Those with information related to the incident may contact the Kuching district police headquarters at 082-244444 or the investigating officer, Insp Logeswara, at 018-2914239.

items.title: Sibu latest to record unhealthy API as nine Sarawak areas affected
items.summary: Meanwhile, 46 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while 13 areas recorded good air quality. API readings from 0 to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and readings above 300 are hazardous. API data is released hourly from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: After Tabung Haji, Anwar says King wants Felda probe next
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 15 — The government will investigate issues involving Felda after completing its probe into alleged misappropriation at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. “The King told me last week that do not let it end with TH, (but) continue,” Anwar said in his policy speech. “Let the enforcement agencies investigate professionally," he said.
